points.description: States the difference: a function prototype (declaration) gives only the signature (name, return type, parameter types) without the body, while the function definition contains the actual body/implementation of the function.
points.partial_credit: Award about 2.5 to 3 marks if only one half is given correctly (e.g., prototype is just the signature/declaration, or definition has the body) without the contrast.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying, in any wording, that the prototype gives the signature/declaration (name, return type, parameters) and the definition contains the actual body/code. Part marks if only one side is stated correctly or the answer is vague (e.g., 'prototype declares, definition implements'). No marks for answers that do not address signature versus body.
